## Pull request overview This PR updates Verus specifications and proofs across the MM/page-table code to eliminate `admit()` usage, mainly by strengthening pre/postconditions and adding lemmas that connect page-table metadata to entry-owner invariants. **Changes:** - Strengthen mapping preconditions in `VmSpace`/page-table cursor specs (including region/metadata constraints) and remove `admit()`-based assertions. - Improve huge-page split proof in `Entry::split_if_mapped_huge` by adding lemmas (`last_pte_implies_frame_match`, `huge_frame_split_child_at`) and tightening `EntryOwner` invariants. - Refine PTE “absent” properties (e.g., absent entries are not `last` for levels > 1) and make `UserPtConfig::item_into_raw_spec` concrete. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 7 out of 7 changed files in this pull request and generated 3 comments.
Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | ostd/src/mm/vm_space.rs | Tightens `map_item_requires` (adds regions + metadata predicates), removes `admit()` in map proof, and concretizes `item_into_raw_spec`. | | ostd/src/mm/page_table/node/entry.rs | Replaces `admit()`s in huge-page split path with explicit lemmas/invariants and threads placeholder slot perms via regions. | | ostd/src/mm/page_table/mod.rs | Strengthens `PageTableEntryTrait::new_properties` to rule out `absent.is_last(level)` for `level > 1`. | | ostd/src/mm/page_table/cursor/mod.rs | Adds a proved postcondition connecting `StrayPageTable` errors to `item_into_raw(item).1 > 1` and strengthens the proof accordingly. | | ostd/src/mm/page_table/cursor/locking.rs | Adjusts lock-range specs and proof structure to remove `admit()`; changes tracked arguments for DFS lock acquisition. | | ostd/specs/mm/virt_mem_example.rs | Updates example spec call site for the new `map_item_requires(..., regions)` signature. | | ostd/specs/mm/page_table/node/entry_owners.rs | Strengthens `EntryOwner` invariants and adds new lemmas used to prove huge-page split behavior; extends `placeholder_slot_perm` axiom with region constraints. |

nodes.bodyHTML:
Pull request overview

This PR updates Verus specifications and proofs across the MM/page-table code to eliminate admit() usage, mainly by strengthening pre/postconditions and adding lemmas that connect page-table metadata to entry-owner invariants.

Changes:

  • Strengthen mapping preconditions in VmSpace/page-table cursor specs (including region/metadata constraints) and remove admit()-based assertions.
  • Improve huge-page split proof in Entry::split_if_mapped_huge by adding lemmas (last_pte_implies_frame_match, huge_frame_split_child_at) and tightening EntryOwner invariants.
  • Refine PTE “absent” properties (e.g., absent entries are not last for levels > 1) and make UserPtConfig::item_into_raw_spec concrete.

Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 7 out of 7 changed files in this pull request and generated 3 comments.

Show a summary per file
File Description
ostd/src/mm/vm_space.rs Tightens map_item_requires (adds regions + metadata predicates), removes admit() in map proof, and concretizes item_into_raw_spec.
ostd/src/mm/page_table/node/entry.rs Replaces admit()s in huge-page split path with explicit lemmas/invariants and threads placeholder slot perms via regions.
ostd/src/mm/page_table/mod.rs Strengthens PageTableEntryTrait::new_properties to rule out absent.is_last(level) for level > 1.
ostd/src/mm/page_table/cursor/mod.rs Adds a proved postcondition connecting StrayPageTable errors to item_into_raw(item).1 > 1 and strengthens the proof accordingly.
ostd/src/mm/page_table/cursor/locking.rs Adjusts lock-range specs and proof structure to remove admit(); changes tracked arguments for DFS lock acquisition.
ostd/specs/mm/virt_mem_example.rs Updates example spec call site for the new map_item_requires(..., regions) signature.
ostd/specs/mm/page_table/node/entry_owners.rs Strengthens EntryOwner invariants and adds new lemmas used to prove huge-page split behavior; extends placeholder_slot_perm axiom with region constraints.

review_comments.body: `lock_range` now assumes `try_traverse_and_lock_subtree_root` returns `Some` and immediately asserts it. At runtime, `try_traverse_and_lock_subtree_root` can return `None` when it detects a stray node (`if is_stray { return None; }`), so this can panic instead of retrying as the doc comment describes. Please reintroduce the retry loop (or otherwise handle `None`) rather than asserting success unconditionally.

review_comments.body: The spec for `try_traverse_and_lock_subtree_root` now states `ensures r is Some`, but the (external_body) implementation explicitly returns `None` on stray detection. This makes the specification unsound for verification and also encourages callers to treat `None` as impossible. Either weaken the postcondition to allow `None` (and preserve invariants/regions in that case), or change the implementation to truly guarantee `Some` (e.g., via a retry loop that can’t fail under the given preconditions).

review_comments.body: `lock_range` no longer guarantees key postconditions (cursor invariants / `in_locked_range` / `level < guard_level`) that callers rely on (e.g., `Cursor::new`’s success-case `ensures`). With the current `ensures` only stating `level <= guard_level`, downstream proofs and APIs that assume the stronger properties won’t be able to use the result soundly. Consider restoring the previous postconditions (and proving them), or update all callers’ specs to match and add explicit proofs where needed.

review_comments.body: `placeholder_slot_perm` is an axiom that can be invoked for any aligned `paddr` with only `regions.inv()` as a precondition, but its postconditions assert facts about `regions.slot_owners[frame_to_index(paddr)]` (e.g., `ref_count != REF_COUNT_UNUSED` and `path_if_in_pt is None`) that are not guaranteed by `regions.inv()` and are false for many valid slots (unused slots, or slots already mapped in the page table). This makes the logic inconsistent (callers could derive contradictions from a valid `regions`). Consider moving these slot-state facts from `ensures` into `requires` (and prove them at the call site), or weakening/removing them from `ensures` so the axiom only provides the permission shape/address properties.
